history.p: The cantata is one of Scheibe's early works. The dating appearing on the manuscript might be read as either 1744 or 1734; the latter year would indicate Leipzig as Scheibe was still there at that time. However, if 1744 is correct then Scheibe was employed as Kapellmeister in Copenhagen; his title of address nearly always appears together with his name after his employment in 1740. The dating also mentions Hamburg, and unless Scheibe was visiting Hamburg in the late summer of 1744 the indication of city is most likely erroneous. Nevertheless, the cantata was presumably commissioned by Carl Gotthelf Gerlach to whom Scheibe even provided music after his employment at the Danish court (cf. Scheibe’s letter to Gottsched, April 1743). According to Glöckner (1990) the work was performed in the Neukirche, Leipzig, by Gerlach on 29 September 1744. When Gerlach died in 1761, the work was acquired by Breitkopf together with a large number of other works and listed in the publisher’s sales catalogue of that year; however, it is not found in later sales catalogues perhaps due to declining popularity of church cantatas. It appears again in Breitkopf’s final auction catalogue of 1836 and was bought by the music collector Carl Ferdinand Becker in Leipzig. The part material has apparently not survived.
